title: Gyro aiming
line: Turns on the motion sensor so you can aim by tilting the Claw.
symptom: The Claw 8 EX's IMU sits behind the Intel sensor hub with MSI firmware Linux doesn't load, so there is no gyro.
why: MSI's Panther Lake ISH firmware (installed under this model's own ish_ptl_<vendor>_<product>.bin name) and the 2247-byte sensor descriptor of board MS-1T91; Lunar Lake and Meteor Lake Claws use other sensor hubs.
risk_note: Installs MSI's own sensor-hub firmware (downloaded from MSI, checked by sha256) and changes boot configuration. Only loads on this exact board.

changes.detail: MSI's sensor-hub firmware under this model's own name, downloaded from MSI and checked by size and sha256.
Adds a firmware search path (shared with the VRR fix).
The firmware file, for an early-loading sensor hub.
A HID-BPF program that labels the hub's sensors as accelerometer and gyro.
Keep the sensor powered and correct its drift.
Adds the gyro as a motion source.

undo: Stops and removes both services, the HID-BPF program, the firmware file, its initramfs entry and the kernel argument (when the VRR fix doesn't need it), and rebuilds the InputPlumber override without the gyro.

probe.what: Looks for a gyro (gyro_3d) that works without GameCove's firmware and HID-BPF program. With the fix in place that can't be told apart, so new linux-firmware and kernel releases are checked by a maintainer.

watch.note: Kernel sensor-hub driver: native support for the Claw's custom sensors would replace the HID-BPF program.
linux-firmware may start shipping MSI's Panther Lake ISH firmware (intel/ish/).
The stock config: an imu source there means InputPlumber expects a native gyro.
A BIOS update can change the sensor hub's firmware needs.
